column2: agreed merge:capítulo, but capitular (423) and capitulares (237) are the real verb and adjective (sala capitular, capitular ante); merging them into capítulo hides a second real word
agreed merge:combo, but combado/combada/combarse are the real verb combar (to bend); check whether the verb share is large enough to keep
agreed merge:enserio, but enserio is a misspelling of the phrase en serio, not a Spanish lemma; target looks wrong (merge into serio, or drop)
agreed drop, but paciendo/pacían (233) are the real verb pacer (to graze); Pace/Pacer are names, the verb should keep
agreed drop as BOJ (Bank of Japan), but lowercase boj (95) is the real Spanish noun boj (boxwood)
agreed drop as the Uros people, but uro/uros is also the Spanish noun for the aurochs; check the lowercase share
agreed drop, but híper is colloquial Spanish for hipermercado and a stand-alone prefix-word; examples only show one reading
agreed keep, but Spanish writes neoyorquino; per the spelling rules a misspelling merges (merge:neoyorquino) unless neoyorkino is the form people write
